text:
Good night, my love, and until tomorrow!

Until tomorrow, yes, when dawn breaks,

and I, after forty years

of incoherent dreaming, open and rub

the eyes of the spirit,

like one who has slept a very, very long time,

and slowly begins to awaken,

and, in a progressive lucidity,

ties the threads of yesterday in my soul

(before the flesh bound it)

to the prodigious today

in which I shall find myself, on this plane

where nothing is illusion and everything

is truth...


Good night, my love,

good night! I remain in darkness

and you flew toward dawn...

Until tomorrow, love, until tomorrow!


For even if destiny

were to pile five-year spans upon five-year spans

of my lifelong imprisonment, those spans

are fleeting; the days follow one another

like rosaries whose great beads

are Sundays...


They are Sundays on which, with my flowers,

I go unfailingly to the cemetery

where your beloved forms lie.

How many bouquets of flowers

have I carried to the grave? I do not know.

How many must I carry? Perhaps only a few now.

Perhaps only a few! Oh, what a delightful prospect!


Perhaps the jailer

is approaching with his ringing keys

to open my cell forever!

Is it perhaps the echo of his steps

that can be heard, moving through the quiet corridors

beyond the window?


Good night, love of my loves!

Until later, perhaps... or until tomorrow.

translation.title: Bonsoir
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves the address “Bonsoir,” the prison-and-cemetery imagery, and the speaker’s ambiguous hope for release.
